record.summary: Arjun Das, a 31‑year‑old senior sales manager with four years of service and a top‑performer award, faced age‑related comments and exclusion after a new regional director took over eight months ago. He raised the issue with HR verbally twice and filed a written complaint on 3 March. Eleven days later he was placed on a performance‑improvement plan (PIP) with targets that depended on accounts already reassigned. On 2 May he was terminated by email for poor performance, received one month’s salary in lieu of notice, and was asked to sign a settlement agreement waiving all claims within seven days. He is unsure whether the termination was retaliatory, whether the age comments amount to discrimination, and whether signing the settlement would forfeit his unvested stock options.
record.goal: Seek guidance on the legality of the termination, the possibility of retaliation or age discrimination, the implications of signing the settlement agreement, and the status of unvested stock options.
questions: What is the calendar year for the dates mentioned (3 March, 14 March, 2 May) to confirm the timeline?
Did HR provide any written response to the formal complaint beyond the acknowledgment? If so, please share the date and content.
Can you share the full text of the settlement agreement draft, especially any clauses about waiving claims and treatment of unvested stock options?
What is the exact vesting schedule for your stock options and how many options remained unvested at the time of termination?
Did you receive any prior written performance warnings or notices before being placed on the PIP?
evidence: Employment contract (30‑day notice clause, stock vesting schedule, confidentiality clause).
Four years of performance reviews and award certificate.
Written complaint to HR with delivery receipt dated 3 March.
Performance Improvement Plan document dated 14 March.
Email from Vikram to junior team member (copied Arjun).
WhatsApp messages from two colleagues about Vikram's "old school" comment.

events.description: Arjun began working as senior sales manager at the logistics software company; received consistently positive reviews and a "top performer" award two years ago.
New regional director Vikram Sethi took over, made comments about Arjun's age and "slow adaptation," excluded him from meetings, and reassigned his key accounts to a junior colleague.
Arjun raised the issue verbally with HR twice.
Arjun sent a formal written complaint to HR alleging discriminatory treatment and a hostile work environment.
events.basis: written complaint to HR with delivery receipt dated 3 March

events.description: HR acknowledged receipt of the complaint but gave no further written response.
Vikram emailed a junior team member, "move his big accounts to you, he's not keeping up with the new tools," copying Arjun.
events.basis: email from Vikram to junior team member (copied Arjun)

events.description: Arjun was placed on a Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) with three targets; two targets depended on accounts already reassigned.

Arjun received a termination email citing poor performance and failure to meet PIP objectives; offered one month’s salary in lieu of notice and a settlement agreement draft requiring signature within seven days.
Settlement agreement draft asks Arjun to waive all claims against the employer.
Arjun has WhatsApp messages from two colleagues stating they heard Vikram describe him as "old school"; colleagues wish to remain unnamed.
Arjun recorded diary notes of the verbal age‑related comments a few weeks after they occurred.
events.basis: diary notes made a few weeks later
